Approaching $x=0$ from the left, we have $x<0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=3sin\,(\frac{\pi }{3}x)+2.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}[3sin\,(\frac{\pi }{3}x)+2] \\  & =3sin\,(\frac{\pi }{3}(0))+2 \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+2 \\  & =3\cdot 0+2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, approaching $x=2$ from the right, we have $x\ge 2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\sqrt{7x+2}-1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}(\sqrt{7x+2}-1) \\  & =\sqrt{7(2)+2}-1 \\  & =\sqrt{16}-1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
